newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's IFI, IFIL sell Fiat stake for Spaolo share.
newsitem.headline: Italy's IFI, IFIL sell Fiat stake for Spaolo share.

text.p: Italy's Agnelli family holdings IFI and IFIL said they are selling San Paolo bank a 2.2 percent stake in Fiat ordinary capital in exchange for a shareholding in San Paolo.
IFI, taking a five percent stake, last week became a core shareholder in San Paolo bank which will be privatised later this year.

The Fiat shares will be transferred to the Compagnia di San Paolo, which indirectly controls Istituto Bancario San Paolo di Torino, on January 15, 1998 at a price of 5,700 lire per share, a statement said.
Both IFI and IFIL have said they wanted to take part in San Paolo's privatisation.
IFI and IFIL are together the largest shareholders in Fiat.
IFI will sell one percent of Fiat capital, or 33.05 million shares, and IFIL will sell 1.2 percent, or 41.15 million shares and will keep first option rights.
After the transfer, IFI and IFIL will hold 30 percent of Fiat's ordinary capital.
